# A stronger ordinary route: consume a preacquired recovery program

30 October2026. C derivation from controlling primary theorems, with
root's independent circuit reconstruction and A's substantive whole
challenge reporting no remaining structural objection. File-bound receipts
are separate. This is not a claim that the least-rank Petz application in
the primary already states our full result.

## 1. What the new primary does and does not supply

Yoshida--Niwa--Utsumi--Takagi--Murao,2512.21260v2, Theorem3/Eq38 supplies
a superchannel converting n parallel calls of one CPTP F:k->B of Kraus rank
at most r into n parallel calls of ONE randomly chosen dilation isometry
V:k->E tensor B, dimE=r. The common random V, not independent draws, is
load-bearing. The proof/actual circuit uses source-input preprocessing;
therefore it cannot be applied retroactively to a received payload to
recover its inaccessible environment. We use it ONLY in offline calibration.

Theorem5, Lemma6 and Eqs44,51 provide a stronger useful program primitive.
For known V0:k->E tensor B, there is a physical offline procedure generating
a joint state with mathematical representation

 integral [P_(V,theta)/k]^tensor n dV dtheta,
 V(theta)=(exp(i theta)|0>V0+|1>V)/sqrt(2),
 P_(V,theta)=V(theta)V(theta)*.                           (O1)

All n copies in(O1) share the SAME V and theta. The controller receives
neither label. The offline circuit is obtained by composing Theorem3 and
Lemma6 and choosing the logical inputs as I_k/k. This is not a product
of separately averaged single-copy programs. The proof representation
can be used in subsequent adaptive channels by linearity, exactly as the
common-frame representation in N1291.

The theorem's direct Petz application, Theorem13/Eqs67--71, is narrower:
r=d_input/d_output, hence a dilation UNITARY and a maximally mixed mean
output. That condition does not hold for a generic expanding approximate
encoder. The route below instead uses Theorem3+5 with the GENERAL Petz
algorithm of Gilyen et al.2006.16924v2, Theorem1.

30October2026. C's finite control admission, using root's controlled-sine
suggestion and ordinary QSVT/oblivious-amplification machinery. This closes
the copy-to-block-encoding port in C_STRONG_ORDINARY_ROUTE.md without
an unknown purification, inverse unitary, or a free "taking logarithms"
oracle. It is deliberately polynomial rather than optimized.

Let S be an unknown density matrix, available as fresh stored copies,
whose NONZERO spectrum is in[mu,1], with public rational0<mu<=1/2.
Its support projector is not given. The input presented to recovery will
lie in this support; every implemented circuit is physical on the whole
carrier, including all zero eigenspaces.

## 1. A bounded native signal from samples

Controlled partial-SWAP simulation, including positive and negative time,
implements controlled exp(plus/minus i S/2). With an ancilla, their
known linear combination

 (exp(i S/2)-exp(-i S/2))/(2i)=sin(S/2)=B

is the top block of a known-format unitary. Public Hadamard/phase gates
and controlled branches supply this block; no postselection is performed
when this unitary is used inside QSVT. Its adjoint is simulated by the
reversed PUBLIC circuit and fresh negative-time sample simulations,
not by attempting to invert a noisy implemented channel.

For the IDEAL signal, occupied eigenvalues lie in[sin(mu/2),sin(1/2)].
Both bounds are separated from0 by at least mu/4. Approximation of every
sample-based unitary call is paid at full reference-safe channel level
over its declared total use count.

# Fixed-rank random-dilation completion and occupied-support recovery

30 October 2026. Independent construction/challenge of the stronger ordinary
route in C_STRONG_ORDINARY_ROUTE.md. It uses established random dilation and
Petz algorithms, with B's copy-acquired filter and the paid growing-rank Schur
port. It is not the primary paper's much narrower least-Kraus-rank Petz corollary.
No source, quantum circuit or numerical model is executed here.

## 1. The actual source is only approximately filtered

Let F be the ideal fixed-threshold filtered channel, with common output support
dimension at most dbar. Kraus rank(F)<=k*dbar because its Choi state is supported
on input-k tensor that output support. The implemented filter Ftilde is close in
diamond norm but can have FULL ambient rank. It is invalid to apply a rank-r
promise directly to Ftilde or to compare normalized postselected objects.

What is needed is ONE fixed physical source-query controller, CPTP on every
possible source, whose promised action on rank-at-most-r F equals the random
dilation construction. Then ordinary channel-query hybrids pay the difference
between Ftilde and F without any claim that Ftilde has rank r.

## 2. A literal post-query completion in the primary circuit

I independently inspected the rendered primary 2512.21260v2 page 7 Figure 2(a),
saved by C at source_entry/C_RDS_FIGURE2.png. Its order is explicit: known
controlled input permutations, ALL source queries, known controlled output
permutations, symmetric-group QFT, MEASUREMENT of lambda, then conditional
preparation of pi_(U_lambda) and inverse small-r Schur transform.

Insert a finite arithmetic test length(lambda)>r immediately before those last
rank-r-dependent operations. On that branch discard/reset all would-be outputs
and prepare any fixed state in the advertised output registers. On valid labels
use the original postprocessor. This is a known measurement/feedforward CPTP
postprocessor for EVERY source. It has no source rank test, no postselected
normalization and no impossible irrep input. Its work is polynomial in the
existing finite labels and output-register count.

For a promised rank-at-most-r source, the normalized Choi random-purification
formula, primary Eqs. 32--37, has zero probability on invalid lambda. The bad
branch is itself a CP map. A CP map with zero Choi trace has positive Choi matrix
of trace zero
